<subject>IAMAI Trade Policy Engagement</subject>
<body>
Everyone,

I finally touched base with Priya Mehta, my contact at the Indian Agricultural & Marketing Industries association ("IAMAI") regarding their involvement on the commodity regulation side, specifically with regard to forward contract licensing.

According to Priya, there is no coordinated group effort that exists (i.e., a commodity committee or an individual state regulator taking the lead on trading policy). Individual state agriculture departments get involved, but that is all. For example, Maharashtra's Vikram Nair recently opposed Agrotech Solutions' application for futures trading approval, but the SEBI still granted Agrotech Solutions' petition.

Priya recommends that we use the state regulators as much as possible. For example, if we believe that local procurement transparency is inadequate and we have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information to the individual state department and have them weigh in on our behalf. Priya recognizes that AgriIndia is market-friendly and that typically the state authorities would be in agreement with our positions - so it's something for us to keep in mind as we move forward. There's no guarantee that SEBI will listen to the state bodies, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral Acharya
Director
Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
Pune
+91-20-6720-8847
